Jordan — thanks, received the diagram. Quick read: overall looks reasonable but there are three areas we need explicit runbook steps for before the first canary:

1) Control plane placement and API endpoints: the control plane must be reachable from your staging cluster over the control-plane peering; we recommend running a dedicated mgmt-subnet with an ALB + mTLS ingress to the control-plane endpoints. We'll provide cert requirements and SNI details.

2) Egress & telemetry: outgoing traffic from inference nodes needs NAT and an egress policy for telemetry/metrics (Prometheus push or pull) and for model artifact fetch. We'll call out ports and IPs your infra must allow.

3) Staged canaries and rollback triggers: we'll propose a 3-step canary: smoke -> small traffic -> scaling test. Each step has explicit health gates (latency, error rate, token drop).

I’ve attached a draft runbook and a staging network map for your team to review. Aditya / Neha — can you validate the control-plane placement recommendation and add any infra caveats (KV cache, local disk access, KMS routing)?

Attachments: vpc-cutover-draft.pdf (attachment stub); staging-network-map.png (attachment stub)

Thanks — happy to jump on a call next week.

Ben Carter

Quick tech notes after a pass over the diagram:

- Control plane: Prefer the control-plane components (api-gateway, scheduler, configstore) in the customer VPC when they require direct access to on-prem identity or proprietary KMS. For your staging split-plane, use a pair of AZ-spread control-plane instances behind an ALB with mTLS. Public endpoints: restrict to Redwood egress IPs and your ops CIDR.

- KV cache/replication: inference nodes run local KV cache to reduce token costs. Ensure the data-plane nodes have low-latency (<=2ms) connectivity to the shared cache primaries or plan a read-replica in the colo. If you can't meet latency, configure cache isolation per-tenant to avoid cross-tenant cold starts.

- Artifact pulls & Caching: allow HTTPS to our artifact CDN and pin cert fingerprint in the runbook for the first cutover. Optionally pre-warm model artifacts in staging to avoid cold-download latency.

- Egress & NAT: The data plane will call back for telemetry (metrics and traces) and for auth token refresh. Provide static NAT IPs for these flows, or use proxying via your ops layer. Also confirm whether your IDS/IPS will inspect TLS — that can break grpc streams.

- Canary gating: define thresholds — 95th pct latency < 220ms, error rate < 0.5%, token failure rate = 0. If a gate fails, rollback step is to revert routing to the previous model variant and scale down the canary pool to zero before cutover window closes.

I'll draft a short canary checklist (canary-checklist.md) and attach.

-Aditya
Principal Infra Architect, Redwood Inference

Adding operational acceptance criteria and a proposed dry-run cadence:

Acceptance criteria (staging -> canary):
- Connectivity: control-plane API reachable from staging nodes (TLS handshake < 200ms).
- Observability: metrics and traces flowing into Redwood's observability collector and your Prometheus (verify two-way).
- Auth: token refresh succeeds for 10000 requests over 10 minutes with no auth error spikes.
- Artifact integrity: models pre-warmed in staging and a single inference run validated against golden prompt set.

Dry-run cadence:
- Day 0 (dry run): deploy control-plane in staging, validate connectivity, run smoke tests (0 traffic).
- Day 1 (canary-1): 1% production traffic for 1 hour, metrics/alerts monitored.
- Day 2 (canary-2): 10% production traffic for 2 hours with load test ramp.
- Day 3 (scale test): 100% scaled load for 30 minutes in a controlled window then revert.

Note: For all canaries, we need documented rollback checks (we'll add steps in canary-checklist.md) and a single owner who can revert routing.

- Data residency: confirm whether any model artifacts or logs are subject to retention policies that require residency in your region. If so, we need to flag this with our Privacy team before cutover.
- Contractual window: your procurement team asked for a 72-hour change freeze after each canary; that will affect our planned daily cadence. Please confirm.

If procurement requires longer freeze windows, we'll adjust the cutover plan above. Happy to coordinate introductions to Procurement and Legal if needed.
